data.why: test_indent.txt is the repository's own fixture in the exact .txt format load_txt() expects (timestamp line, 'Number of Points =' line, tab-separated Depth/Load/Time header and numeric block).

goals: Upload a raw load-depth indentation curve and confirm it parses correctly (points, min/max load, timestamp)
Preprocess the curve (remove pre-contact noise, rescale depth, find the contact point) and compare raw vs. processed overlays
Run and compare multiple pop-in detectors (Isolation Forest, CNN autoencoder, Fourier derivative, Savitzky-Golay) and see where they agree or disagree
Identify confident pop-in events (flagged by 2+ methods) versus single-method detections worth manual inspection
Compute load-depth pop-in statistics (depth jump, pop-in length) and stress-strain statistics (stress/strain jump and slope) for detected events
Download annotated CSVs, plots, and a ZIP bundle of results and configuration for later reporting

review.summary: The tree follows the README's load → preprocess → detect-and-compare → quantify → export pipeline closely, and most cited screens match what the nodes say. The default-only detector run is reported honestly. It needs small fixes before filing: t3 cites a screen with the advanced-thresholds expander closed, t6/t7 have inaccurate general labels and t6 hides the all-None load-depth table, and the detector-tuning comparison loop and metadata preview are missing.
